questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A smaller university in a English speaking country outside of Europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had some interesting courses at UVic and I lived with amazing roommates. It was definitely a fun experience. However, I did not have much time to explore because my work burden was very tough. This would have been fine if there had been structure but I had a professor (the same one in two of my courses) who was extremely unstructured and put a lot pressure on all the students. He got quite a lot of negative feedback from the students I studied with and apparently this is not the first time he has gotten that. He definitely did not make it easy to study in a new environment.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was sent a lot of introduction emails of where to find information and there was a couple of days of very nice introduction before school started. It made the transition quite easy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. I used Facebook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky to find housing with people my own age. Most of the exchange students were living with families.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is a long process but pretty easy to figure out and a lot of help to get.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: 1. Read the course descriptions and find the ones you like. 2. Make a schedule on the university's website so you can see there are no schedule clashes. 3. Apply to get the prerequisites for the classes approved by Uvic. 4. Receive an official time to apply for the classes. 5. Apply at the time you are given.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Team meetings and emailing.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was easy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Participate in the online meetings and you will get all the information you need.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had one really amazing course and professor in it. But I also had one professor in two of my courses who made the semester stressful - he was extremely unstructured.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were the same level as at UCPH but two of my courses were very unstructured and thus made it a lot harder.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style was unstructured and especially one of my pressors seemed very unprepared. It mostly felt like he was just there because he had to be.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Monetary Policy and Theory
Money and Banking
Financial Economics
Business Analysis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Monetary Policy and Theory is a great course with a very dedicated professor. Pick this if you like macro. Money and Banking is also a very interesting course - I was just unlucky with my professor.
